title: HfO2/SiO2 with Quarter-Wave Initialized Phase-Aligned Optimization at 21 Layers
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing all alternating-index layers as exact quarter-wave optical thickness at the passband midpoint (267.5 nm) and applying a phase-alignment penalty during early optimization stages will improve constructive interference in the UV passband while maintaining visible/NIR blocking, yielding higher target scores than the unseeded 15-layer defect cavity approach.
design_principle: Physics-guided initialization: construct alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs as λ/4 layers at 267.5 nm using estimated effective indices (n_HfO2≈2.1, n_SiO2≈1.5 at 267 nm), then apply bounded differential evolution with augmented penalty term for optical path length deviations before allowing free thickness variation.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused silica (21 finite layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses (21 variables, initialized to quarter-wave values at 267.5 nm)
Optimization algorithm: differential evolution with phase-alignment penalty in early generations
manufacturing_considerations: Quarter-wave initialization may improve thickness reproducibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectivity mirrors
Phase alignment for constructive interference in passband
expected_advantages: Improved UV passband transmission through phase coherence
Maintained visible/NIR blocking from increased layer count vs 15-layer baseline
known_risks: HfO2 absorption may increase below 280 nm
Quarter-wave initialization may trap optimizer in local minimum
21 layers may still be insufficient for broad visible/NIR blocking
execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 21-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused silica. Initialize all layer thicknesses as quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5 nm wavelength (t_HfO2 = 267.5/(4*2.1) ≈ 31.8 nm, t_SiO2 = 267.5/(4*1.5) ≈ 44.6 nm). Optimize using bounded differential evolution with penalty term proportional to deviation from quarter-wave optical path lengths during first 50 generations, then allow free thickness variation. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, suppress transmittance 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Total layer count exactly 21. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive from iteration_01: replace unseeded initialization with physics-guided quarter-wave seed at 267.5 nm band midpoint, add phase-alignment penalty during early optimization, increase layer count from 15 to 21 to explore additional blocking capability.
